title: Spicy Peanut Noodles with Ground Pork and Shredded Vegetables
description: Grated carrots, squash, and chopped mint balance the spicy heat of the jalapeños. For a milder dish, use only 1 chile and remove its seeds and ribs—they’re hotter than the flesh itself.
ingredients: 1/2 lb. dried 1/4-inch-wide rice noodles (pad thai noodles)
1/2 cup crunchy peanut butter, preferably natural
1 or 2 jalapeños, stemmed and finely chopped (seeded, if desired)
2 large yellow squash or zucchini (about 1 lb.), grated
Lime wedges, maybe some siracha, for serving
directions: Heat 2 tsp. of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the pork, garlic, ginger, and ½ tsp. salt and cook, stirring to break up the meat, until just cooked through, 4 to 6 minutes; set aside.
If you like your vegetables a little cooked, add them to the pork mixture so they “steam” a little for a few minutes.
In a large bowl, whisk the peanut butter, vinegar, fish sauce, the remaining 1 tsp. oil, and 3 Tbs. warm water until smooth.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the rice noodles and cook, stirring often, until just tender, about 5 minutes. Drain and rinse under warm water.
Add the drained noodles, pork, jalapeños, scallions, carrots, squash, and all but 2 Tbs. of the mint and toss gently.
Garnish with the remaining mint and serve at room temperature with the lime wedges on the side.
